newsitem.title: USA: Network misses $1 EPS target, shrs returned.
newsitem.headline: Network misses $1 EPS target, shrs returned.

text.p: Network Long Distance Inc said Thursday it did not hit an earnings target of $1 a share for fiscal 1997.

As a result, 313,344 shares of its common stock held in escrow since 1994 have been returned to the company treasury for cancellation. The move represents a cut in total outstanding common stock of about 2.3 percent.

The company said in a statement that the shares were held by co-founder Marc Becker, who had an escrow pact providing for the return of the shares if the company did not hit an earnings of $1 a share for fiscal 1997.
"The company did not hit the earnings target," Network's statement said.
First Call estimates for the company's fiscal 1997 earnings were not immediately available.

The company said it has accepted the board resignations of Becker and Joseph Edelman. Becker resigned to pursue other interests but Edelman will continue to assist in integrating the company with its recent acquisitions, the company said.
It also said it has additional shares in escrow previously held by its former chief executive, Michael Ross, that were not returned.
It said Ross recently filed a lawsuit to block the return of the shares to the company treasury.

"The company believes the lawsuit is without merit and will vigorously defend its long-stated position that the shares would be returned to the company if it did not meet the targeted earnings for the fiscal year ended March 31," the company statement said.
No one at the company offices returned a call for further information Thursday evening.

Louisiana-based Network Long Distance is an interexchange carriers offering digital switch-based and switchless fiber optic telecommunications services to commercial customers, trade association/affinity program members, third-party independent agents and other long distance companies.
